column1: # Step 3 (03-spark-32): the gate, composed.
# Seven lines, and three of them are new shapes on this ladder.
#   common.tsv   the standing rules -- true of the untouched tree, so a FAIL is
#                a void reading rather than an unmigrated one
#   floor.tsv    the two standing rules whose thresholds are this codebase's
#   cheats.tsv   the nine ways to fake a step on this ladder, priced at the
#                whole reward
#   cheats3.tsv  the nine that are step 3's own, at the same price. Split from
#                cheats.tsv rather than added to it because step 2's instruction
#                does not state them, and a prohibition the instruction does not
#                state is a trap. score.py reads both files.
#   m01.tsv      *held*: step 1's requirements become preconditions. Two of them
#                are false at this rung and m03.tsv restates them -- see the
#                overrides at the top of that file, and step02.tsv's header,
#                which predicted this step by name.
#   m02.tsv      *held*: step 2's requirements likewise. Nothing in it is
#                rung-sensitive -- every rule reads Dataset/RDD bytecode or
#                probe.job rows -- so it carries across the fence unchanged.
#                This is also where step 3's two run-integrity checks come from:
#                `held-replay-probed` (the replay ran with the listener
#                attached) and `held-probe-submit-clean` (nothing this verifier
#                submitted failed). They are not restated here, because a second
#                copy under a second name would report the same fact twice in a
#                report a human reads. Any later step that drops `hold m02.tsv`
#                must restate them, or its gate will be green on a run that
#                never happened.
#                One sentence of m02.tsv's header stopped being true here:
#                `probe-submit-clean`'s reason says common.tsv's
#                `probe-submit-ok` is satisfied by the control run alone. As of
#                round 1 of step 3's item-5 review, step 3's test.sh no longer
#                feeds the verifier's own control run to the gate at all (the
#                reasoning is in test.sh, section 6). The rule is unchanged and
#                still worth holding -- "a submit happened" and "none of them
#                failed" remain different claims -- but at this step the second
#                one is no longer the only one that reads the candidate's run.
#   rung3.tsv    the three engine preconditions this rung brings with it,
#                standing rather than graded -- item 4.3 measured every one of
#                them green on a tree that changed nothing, because the replay
#                runs the image's Spark and not the pom's. Read that file's
#                header before moving one of them back.
#   cheats3.tsv  the nine prohibitions that undo this rung, priced at the whole
#                reward. score.py reads this file by name alongside cheats.tsv.
#                Seven of them until round 2 of the item-5 review: the two
#                adaptive-execution switches were read off the engine only, and
#                every other prohibition here has a second, independent read.
#                They now have their `setconf` twin.
#   m03.tsv      m1 and m2, the requirements weights.tsv pays for.
# Order matters: the overrides in m03.tsv replace rules that `hold m01.tsv`
# defines, and rules.py requires an override's target to already exist.
include common.tsv
include floor.tsv
include cheats.tsv
include cheats3.tsv
include rung3.tsv
hold m01.tsv
hold m02.tsv
include m03.tsv
include m03-inherit.tsv
